title: Lens Use Explanation
description: Essential Criteria: Clearly explain that visible light can be focused with glass lenses while X-rays require crystals for refraction.

title: Mirror Use Explanation
description: Essential Criteria: Describe how X-rays can only be reflected at critical angles, unlike visible light which can be reflected by common mirrors.

title: Chromatic Resolving Power
description: Important Criteria: Discuss the relationship between wavelength and chromatic resolving power, noting that it is narrower for X-rays.

title: Minimum Angular Separation
description: Important Criteria: Explain that the minimum resolvable angular separation is smaller for X-rays due to their shorter wavelength.

title: Unit Consistency
description: Optional Criteria: Ensure that all units are consistent and correctly applied throughout the response.

title: Common Errors
description: Pitfall Criteria: Watch for incorrect statements about the use of lenses or mirrors for X-rays, which may lead to misunderstandings.

title: Wavelength Misunderstanding
description: Pitfall Criteria: Avoid confusion between the properties of visible light and X-rays, particularly regarding their interaction with materials.
